\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مهنة} (mihna)}{مهنة (mihna)}]{\ar{مهنة} (mihna) — a profession, a trade}

\label{lesson:AR-C518-mihna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to get hungry, then the Arabic for to be full.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مهنة}}
\textbf{\ar{مهنة}} — \emph{mihna} — \textquotedblleft{}a profession, a trade\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{مهنة} \ar{أبي} \ar{التدريس}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mihnat abī at-tadrīs.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father's profession is teaching.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{مهن}, \emph{mihan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مهنة}} (\emph{mihna}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{m-h-n}, \textquotedblleft{}to serve, to work\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Mihna is the work one serves at.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mihna}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mihna}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mihnat abī at-tadrīs.} — My father's profession is teaching.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to get hungry, then the Arabic for to be full, then say \emph{mihna} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{مهنة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A profession, a trade\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{سكرتير} (sikritīr)}{سكرتير (sikritīr)}]{\ar{سكرتير} (sikritīr) — a secretary}

\label{lesson:AR-C518-sikritir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to be full, then the Arabic for a profession.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{سكرتير}}
\textbf{\ar{سكرتير}} — \emph{sikritīr} — \textquotedblleft{}a secretary\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تعمل} \ar{أختي} \ar{سكرتيرة} \ar{في} \ar{شركة} \ar{كبيرة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taʿmalu ukhtī sikritīra fī sharika kabīra.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My sister works as a secretary in a big company.
\end{quote}

The feminine is \ar{سكرتيرة}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{سكرتير}} (\emph{sikritīr}) is a modern loan, usually traced to Italian \emph{segretario} or French \emph{secrétaire}, words that go back to Latin \emph{secretum}, \textquotedblleft{}a secret\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sikritīr}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taʿmalu ukhtī sikritīra fī sharika kabīra.} — My sister works as a secretary in a big company.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to be full, then the Arabic for a profession, then say \emph{sikritīr} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{سكرتير} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A secretary\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{بيطري} (bayṭarī)}{بيطري (bayṭarī)}]{\ar{بيطري} (bayṭarī) — a vet}

\label{lesson:AR-C518-baytari}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a profession, then the Arabic for a secretary.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{بيطري}}
\textbf{\ar{بيطري}} — \emph{bayṭarī} — \textquotedblleft{}a vet\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{عالج} \ar{البيطري} \ar{الحصان} \ar{المريض}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ʿālaja al-bayṭarī al-ḥiṣān al-marīḍ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The vet treated the sick horse.
\end{quote}

The full phrase is \ar{طبيب} \ar{بيطري}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{بيطري}} (\emph{bayṭarī}) is built on \emph{bayṭār}, an old word for a horse doctor, which was borrowed from Greek \emph{hippiatros}, \textquotedblleft{}horse doctor\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB). The ending \emph{-ī} makes it \textquotedblleft{}of the bayṭār\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bayṭarī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bayṭarī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿālaja al-bayṭarī al-ḥiṣān al-marīḍ.} — The vet treated the sick horse.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a profession, then the Arabic for a secretary, then say \emph{bayṭarī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{بيطري} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A vet\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مستشار} (mustashār)}{مستشار (mustashār)}]{\ar{مستشار} (mustashār) — an adviser, a consultant}

\label{lesson:AR-C518-mustashar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a secretary, then the Arabic for a vet.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مستشار}}
\textbf{\ar{مستشار}} — \emph{mustashār} — \textquotedblleft{}an adviser, a consultant\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{يعمل} \ar{خالي} \ar{مستشارا} \ar{في} \ar{شركة} \ar{كبيرة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yaʿmalu khālī mustashāran fī sharika kabīra.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My uncle works as an adviser in a big company.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مستشار}} (\emph{mustashār}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{sh-w-r}, \textquotedblleft{}to point out; to take counsel\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Mustashār is the one whose counsel is sought (Form X).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{طمح} (ṭamaḥa)}{طمح (ṭamaḥa)}]{\ar{طمح} (ṭamaḥa) — to aspire}

\label{lesson:AR-C518-tamaha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a vet, then the Arabic for an adviser.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{طمح}}
\textbf{\ar{طمح}} — \emph{ṭamaḥa} — \textquotedblleft{}to aspire\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{يطمح} \ar{ابني} \ar{إلى} \ar{أن} \ar{يصبح} \ar{طيارا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yaṭmaḥu ibnī ilā an yuṣbiḥa ṭayyāran.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My son aspires to become a pilot.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يطمح}, \emph{yaṭmaḥ}.

It takes \ar{إلى}. Ṭumūḥ, ambition, which you know, is its noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{طمح}} (\emph{ṭamaḥa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ṭ-m-ḥ}, \textquotedblleft{}to raise the eyes towards\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Lane gives ṭamaḥa of the sight, raised towards a thing.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭamaḥa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭamaḥa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yaṭmaḥu ibnī ilā an yuṣbiḥa ṭayyāran.} — My son aspires to become a pilot.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a vet, then the Arabic for an adviser, then say \emph{ṭamaḥa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{طمح} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To aspire\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
